description: Portable processor scenarios for the OpenAPI 2.0 binding-specification sibling. Configuration is named semantically; adapters normalize HTTP observations.

scenarios.description: OAS 2.0 Parameter Object text states that a body parameter's name has no effect on the parameter itself and that only one payload exists (edition analysis N2-09). The caller therefore supplies the JSON value once in body, and the declared name payload never appears on the wire [CO20-03].

The exact binding token owns the Swagger 2.0 gate: a compatible-looking swagger value refuses at load even when a valid-looking OpenAPI 3.x discriminator is also present, and the processor never falls through to the sibling lane.

Once swagger is exactly 2.0, a co-present OpenAPI 3.x discriminator is only an unknown Swagger field: it does not steal the source into another lane or destroy an otherwise resolvable source, so the absent selected method refuses at resolution rather than load.
A YAML stream containing a second document refuses at the closed accepted-representation grammar gate; the first document is never silently selected.
Selector evaluation never percent-decodes its RFC 6901 path token: a percent-encoded rendering remains a distinct, unresolvable target.

A selected external Path Item reference resolves relative to the co-present source location, follows the target resource's fragment graph, detects its alternating cycle without resource exhaustion, and refuses before dispatch.

A cross-location name collision selects qualified mode for every non-body caller key; path and query values use uppercase UTF-8 percent encoding, the qualified header name uses RFC 6901 escaping only in the envelope, and configured boolean conversion supplies its exact header value.
Query collectionFormat multi emits one contribution per member, preserves member order, and percent-encodes each member without changing the repeated structural pairs.
A pipes array preserves the structural pipe while percent-encoding member data independently.
A converted csv member containing the structural comma is ambiguous and refuses before dispatch.
An admitted empty query string with emptyValueForm name-only emits the exact parameter name without an equals sign.
The sibling admitted empty spelling is selected explicitly as a present empty value and emits the equals sign.

No binding default chooses between distinct empty spellings, so an empty supplied string without `emptyValueForm` is context-required before dispatch. Supplying the named point makes the same invocation proceed; nothing reaches the wire while it is missing.
A caller header value containing CR and LF refuses before the peer can observe request splitting bytes.
An unknown caller parameter key is never passed through, even when the selected operation declares no parameters.
The upstream-illegal coexistence of effective body and formData parameters removes the selected operation as invalid independently of input.
A required caller parameter remains missing when only an artifact default exists; the processor never inserts that default.
A path expression without the exact effective path parameter excludes the target before caller input is inspected.
The draft-04 integer pin is lexical: a caller JSON number written 1.0 does not satisfy integer even when conversion is configured.
JSON null is present rather than omission and becomes usable only through the deterministic parameterConversion result.
A supplied boolean without a configured conversion result refuses before dispatch rather than acquiring an implementation-defined spelling.

An Operation parameter overrides a Path Item parameter only at its exact name-plus-location identity; the optional string replacement therefore permits omission of the required integer declaration it replaced.
Two effective header names differing only by ASCII case exclude the target because their distinct declarations collapse onto one HTTP field identity.
An envelope top-level member outside parameters and body refuses before dispatch even for a parameter-free target.
Inline non-body assertions remain active before serialization, so an integer below minimum refuses before conversion or dispatch.
A required body Parameter is supplied only by presence of the envelope body member; its documentary Parameter name cannot satisfy omission and no parameters-map key substitutes for it.

Two usable concrete consumes alternatives preserve both choices; a required body therefore needs an explicit `requestMedia` choice before input consumption, and the supplied value never elects. The missing named point is context-required and nothing reaches the wire until it is supplied.
A normalized collision excludes only that media identity; the surviving non-colliding concrete JSON alternative is the sole usable candidate and self-selects independently of list order.
An omitted optional body is no payload: it bypasses an otherwise ambiguous consumes set and emits neither representation bytes nor Content-Type.
A body string with format binary is the OpenBindings raw-octet lane: canonical Base64 decodes before dispatch even for a concrete image media type.
A body string with format byte is already artifact-encoded Base64 characters; it is sent as text and is never decoded a second time by the raw-octet boundary.

Swagger formData selected as application/x-www-form-urlencoded uses the HTML 4.01 UTF-8 algorithm, preserving multi member order, SPACE as plus, uppercase percent triplets, and the chosen name-only empty spelling.
A formData file parameter makes application/x-www-form-urlencoded unusable because that lane cannot carry file bytes; the required payload refuses before dispatch.
Multipart emits one exact-name file part with raw decoded octets and its concrete propertyMedia Content-Type, while inventing neither filename nor Content-Transfer-Encoding.
A present multipart file needs one concrete `propertyMedia` choice keyed by the file parameter name. The missing named point is context-required and nothing dispatches until it is supplied.
A nonempty success response selects its concrete Content-Type through effective produces and strict JSON-decodes the governing response schema as the one operation value.
A response schema with format binary carries exact response octets across the OpenBindings boundary as canonical Base64.
A nonempty response without Content-Type assumes application/octet-stream before ordinary produces matching, then uses the schema-selected raw-octet lane.
A governing Response Object without schema declares no response content, so an actual nonempty body is a loud protocol error after dispatch.
A nonempty response whose Content-Type matches no effective produces declaration is a loud protocol error; body bytes never invent a fallback lane.
text/json is outside the JSON lane and uses character data only when the response declaration admits string as its sole non-null type.
The actual request and response Content-Encoding fields both name identity, which is a no-op requiring no runtime codec; both representation byte sequences remain unchanged.

A caller-supplied request Content-Encoding token admitted by its Header Parameter but unsupported by runtime encoder capability is never skipped or sniffed: a request-side condition refuses before dispatch.
A supplied body payload on GET is refused before dispatch even when its schema and consumes media would otherwise define bytes; the same operation remains usable without that optional payload.
A present empty Operation consumes list replaces a usable root default; a required body therefore has no admitted media lane and refuses before input consumption.
A concrete requestMedia choice preserves two declared alternatives, matches the vendor JSON alternative exactly, and supplies the emitted Content-Type without consulting the body value.
application/xml does not manufacture an object-to-XML mapping: an object body declaration makes that selected media cell unusable and refuses before dispatch.
application/xml is in the closed character-data set when the body declaration admits only string; absent charset defaults to UTF-8 and the supplied text rides unchanged.
A raw-octet request rejects a padded Base64 spelling with nonzero unused pad bits; decodability alone is weaker than the canonical OpenBindings boundary.
A response string with format byte remains the artifact's Base64-character value and is not re-encoded as an OpenBindings raw-octet value.
A non-2xx final status remains the native failure even when default governs it; the JSON body uses the same media lane and is retained as opaque application failure data, never emitted as output.
Distinct produces entries that normalize to the same media identity make selection through that identity unusable, so a matching response refuses without list-order preference.
Every non-file multipart formData contribution is one exact-name part with fixed text/plain UTF-8 media, without a filename or transfer-encoding invention.
A sole root HTTP scheme combines exactly with the authored host including port, basePath, and Paths key.
An Operation schemes array replaces rather than merges the root schemes array.
Two usable HTTP schemes require an explicit `server` choice and list order supplies no preference. The missing named point is context-required and nothing dispatches until it is supplied.
The server configuration selects the authored effective scheme by zero-based index without rewriting host or basePath.
Absent schemes and host inherit the retrieval scheme and complete authority including port, and an absent basePath contributes no segment.
A WebSocket scheme is unusable, leaving the sole HTTPS alternative to self-select without list-order inference.

An effective list containing only ws and wss has no usable target under the HTTP binding. The unusable-scheme exclusion leaves the effective list empty, and §10 states in its own words that “a complete configured URL below remains the available recovery”. A refusal with a stated recovery through a named point is §3.2's context-required species, not its plain one.

A complete consumer-configured URL replaces the resolved server base, and the operation's path bytes join to it under the preceding boundary rule; the artifact's path template, path substitution, query construction, method, parameters, payload, response, and security semantics remain unchanged.
Target construction removes exactly the redundant slash at the configured-server/Paths-key seam: a trailing server slash and the operation's leading slash produce one slash, not two.
A sole apiKey security requirement self-selects and carries its runtime value at the exact header destination.
A query apiKey value uses the same uppercase RFC 3986 percent encoding as query Parameters.
Basic security constructs the RFC 7617 Authorization value from the named runtime user-id and password.

OAuth2 wire carriage is the Bearer access token alone. The credential names more scopes than the declaration requires, which changes nothing: §11's convention makes scope satisfaction the counterparty's determination, so the binding neither reads nor compares a credential's scope set and dispatches on the token.

A credential naming fewer scopes than the operation declares still dispatches. §11: "Whether a supplied credential satisfies a required scope is the counterparty's own determination and is never evaluated by this binding ... An OAuth 2.0 alternative is complete when its scheme's runtime access token is supplied." No accepted edition assigns a client a verification duty or gives a credential's granted scopes any representation, and the three 3.x siblings state the same convention word for word, so all four lines answer this input identically. A token the counterparty finds insufficient produces that counterparty's own response, classified under §9 like any other.

Multiple security alternatives require an explicit `security` selection even when runtime credentials happen to satisfy one of them. The missing named point is context-required and nothing dispatches until it is supplied.
Selecting a safe security alternative ignores a different alternative whose query destination collides with an effective Parameter.
An omitted optional Parameter emits no destination, so a selected credential with the same declared destination emits once and dispatches.
An Operation security empty array clears the root requirement and unrelated runtime credentials never volunteer onto the wire.

An anonymous empty-AND alternative is complete but receives no preference over a credentialed sibling, so multiple alternatives still require an explicit `security` selection. The missing named point is context-required and nothing dispatches until it is supplied.
Explicitly selecting the anonymous alternative dispatches without a credential even when another alternative is credentialed.
Every scheme in one Security Requirement Object is an AND obligation and non-colliding header and query credentials are both carried.
Operation security replaces the root requirement, so only the operation-selected scheme contributes a credential.

A nonempty requirement array for basic is an upstream-invalid declaration that removes that security alternative from selection before any runtime credential is inspected; with no remaining complete alternative the selected target refuses before credentials can dispatch.
An unknown security-scheme name makes only its selected alternative unusable and never activates an extension-like declaration.
An OAuth2 implicit definition without its required authorizationUrl makes the selected alternative unusable.
An apiKey targeting processor-owned Proxy-Authorization makes the selected security alternative unusable before dispatch; origin credentials never become proxy credentials.
Basic and OAuth2 schemes in one AND requirement collide at Authorization, making that selected alternative unusable.

An effective Accept Header Parameter owns and suppresses generated response-media advertisement, so a credential targeting that same field collides with the effective parameter; without such a parameter, Accept remains binding-owned.
A header apiKey credential containing CR or LF refuses before dispatch instead of reaching the HTTP stack.

Without a configured URL, omitting target defaults in a self-contained document leaves the target unresolved before dispatch. §10 names the recovery for an unresolved target: “a complete configured URL below remains the available recovery”. The refusal therefore names `server` under §12.1 rather than ending the attempt with nothing to act on.

An exact status Response governs before default: the exact 200 declaration admits the actual identity Content-Encoding field, while the default declaration constrains that field to gzip and would produce a protocol error if selected.
An exact failure Response also governs before default. Because the exact 404 declaration has no schema, its actual nonempty body is a protocol error rather than data decoded through default.
A nonempty successful response with neither an exact nor default governing Response is a loud protocol error after dispatch.
The Swagger 2.0 Responses Object has no range-key form, so 2XX is upstream-invalid and removes the selected target before dispatch even though it resembles a later-edition response key.
Every Operation requires a nonempty Responses Object, so omission is upstream-invalid and removes the selected target before dispatch.
A response to HEAD is empty by definition; received message-body bytes are not decoded or emitted, even when the governing Response has no schema.
An empty successful response emits no value and needs no governing Response lookup; the nonempty-only no-governing limit is not broadened to status-only responses.
A declared Location response header on 201 creates no output member; response headers remain protocol metadata outside the unary operation value.
A default Response governs an unmatched non-2xx status; its text lane decodes one opaque application-authored failure value, which is retained as error data and never emitted as output.
A Schema Object containing $ref is a JSON Reference: a conflicting non-$ref sibling, including type, is ignored and the referent alone governs carriage-lane selection.

An absent basePath contributes no path segment: the exact Paths key appends directly to the effective host with no synthetic slash and no double-slash composition, unlike an authored basePath of "/" whose byte is preserved.

An admitted exact key whose value is not a Response Object retains precedence and remains an invalid response alternative, but it does not remove the target; an empty successful response dispatches and completes with no output.
A non-string response description is confined to the unused documentary projection; the valid sibling schema still governs and decodes the successful JSON response.
A non-map response headers member is confined to that invalid projection and imposes no constraint; the valid sibling schema still governs and decodes the successful JSON response.
An invalid governing response schema does not remove the target; an empty successful response dispatches and completes with no output because no body decoding is needed.
A non-map response examples member is confined to unused coverage; the valid sibling schema still governs and decodes the successful JSON response.
A non-Header member of the response headers map is confined to that projection; the valid sibling schema still governs and decodes the successful JSON response.
Omitting the required response description is documentary coverage loss only; the valid sibling schema still governs and decodes the successful JSON response.
A response defect confined to one target does not affect a sibling operation in the same source; selecting the intact sibling still resolves, dispatches, and completes.

The carve-out stated in the same breath as the exclusion: a governing Response Object that omits its REQUIRED `description` while declaring no `schema` loses no representation — nothing it states about a response body is misdeclared — so the target stays represented, the declaration governs, and an empty actual body completes with no output value.

A defect in a Response Object that can never govern a 2xx — here an exact 404 — does not remove the target, because failure data is best-effort. The target whose success path is intact still resolves and dispatches; synthesis separately accounts the invalid 404 Response projection as coverage loss.

An unsupplied OPTIONAL parameter carrying an artifact default is omitted before serialization exactly as one carrying none: default documents what the receiver assumes and is never inserted by the binding.

A supplied zero-member array is an empty value under a join collectionFormat rather than an omission: at a query parameter declaring allowEmptyValue, emptyValueForm name-only emits the exact parameter name without an equals sign.
collectionFormat multi is not exempt: a supplied zero-member array contributes one instance carrying no value, and emptyValueForm empty selects the present-empty spelling.
Because a supplied zero-member array is an empty value and not an omission, a query declaration without allowEmptyValue does not admit it and the invocation refuses before dispatch.
At a path parameter the allowEmptyValue flag is inapplicable, so a supplied zero-member array substitutes as zero characters rather than refusing.
The same inapplicable-flag rule at a header parameter: a supplied zero-member array is carried as the empty field value RFC 9110 admits.

Multipart entity framing: only CRLF represents a line break between body parts, a blank CRLF line terminates each part's headers, and the delimiter that follows a part is preceded by a CRLF that is not part of the content.
The multipart name parameter is emitted as a quoted-string, which is what carries a form parameter name the token production does not admit.

A boundary parameter carried by an effective consumes entry takes part in declaration matching: a requestMedia choice that omits it presents no equal value for a declared parameter and matches nothing, so the invocation refuses before dispatch.
The matching half of the same rule: a requestMedia choice presenting the declared boundary value matches, and the entity is emitted with a boundary parameter on the request media type.
boundary is not charset: its value compares by exact character sequence, so a choice differing only by ASCII case matches no declaration and refuses before dispatch.

charset is the one media-type parameter whose value compares ASCII case-insensitively, so a requestMedia choice spelling it in lower case matches a declaration spelling it in upper case and the request dispatches.
The request Content-Type field carries the elected concrete media type in its parsed form: a mixed-case declaration elects itself and is emitted with type and subtype in lower case.
The rest of the same parsed form: a media-type parameter name is emitted in lower case, and a declared quoted-string value the token production admits is emitted unquoted.

A caller-supplied request value on the raw-octet lane that is not a JSON string at all does not decode, and the invocation refuses before dispatch: no wire fact exists yet, so the loud-protocol-error outcome is unavailable to it.

The same rule on the other non-canonical spelling: required RFC 4648 padding is omitted, so the string is outside the canonical form, no spelling is repaired, and the invocation refuses before dispatch.

A Security Scheme Object whose type is outside the closed basic/apiKey/oauth2 set is upstream-invalid: it removes every alternative naming it as invalid before any runtime credential is inspected, leaving this sole-alternative target with none.
A successful response whose single Content-Type field value is a list of media types selects no media type at all; the binding does not pick a member, and the interaction is a loud protocol error.

The unsuccessful half of the same shape is not a protocol error: the listed Content-Type is an unmatched media type under the best-effort failure-body rule, so the interaction completes unsuccessfully with the native failure and carries no failure-data value.

The effective produces a response reads is the operation-level set: a Response Object declares no produces of its own, so a produces member written inside one contributes nothing and the actual media type it names still matches no declaration.

An unquoted numeric Responses key loads and the operation completes. YAML's Core schema resolves the plain scalar 200 to tag:yaml.org,2002:int, but an OpenAPI document is itself a JSON object that YAML merely represents, so the key is the JSON member name it spells. This is the ordinary OpenAPI YAML idiom.

source.content:
swagger: '2.0'
info:
  title: T
  version: '1'
schemes:
  - https
host: api.example
paths:
  /x:
    get:
      responses:
        204:
          description: ok

scenarios.description: A plain scalar key never refuses on its resolved type, whichever Core-schema tag that resolution assigns: an unquoted true in key position is the member name it spells, and the document loads.

source.content:
swagger: '2.0'
info:
  title: T
  version: '1'
schemes:
  - https
host: api.example
x-vendor:
  true: 1
paths:
  /x:
    get:
      responses:
        '204':
          description: ok

scenarios.description: What refuses at the key gate is a key that is no scalar at all. A sequence in key position is no representation of a JSON member name and refuses at load.

A supplied empty string at a `query` parameter declaring `allowEmptyValue: true` reaches the point where the two admitted empty spellings produce distinct bytes and no binding default prefers one. §8.1 makes `emptyValueForm` a required choice there, so §3.2's refusal is the context-required species: it names the point under §12.1 and carries its closed admissible set, and supplying either member makes the same invocation proceed. Nothing reaches the wire either way.

The same declaration with a non-empty supplied value never reaches the point where the two empty spellings differ, so `emptyValueForm` is not awaited and the invocation dispatches with the ordinary value. The choice's applicability is fixed by the declaration, but the refusal it repairs is reached only by a supplied empty value; naming the point on every invocation at such a parameter would refuse what §8.1 admits.

One usable non-anonymous security alternative with no supplied credential is context-required on that credential before dispatch. The requirement is identified by the artifact's declared scheme name and is distinct from §12.1's configuration points.

Two declared security alternatives require one complete selection before dispatch, and no list-order preference is inferred. The refusal names `security` under §12.1 and carries the point's own boundary: an object selecting one alternative by index. Credentials are not volunteered here, because which alternative's credentials are needed is exactly what the missing choice decides.

Two usable concrete `consumes` alternatives over a required body preserve both declarations and elect neither; §9.1 requires one concrete `requestMedia` choice before input consumption. The refusal is therefore the context-required species and names the point before any supplied value is read, which is also why it precedes every value-conditional point on the same document.

A required `file` form parameter carried as a multipart part needs one concrete media type for that part, and §12.1 makes it the conditional `propertyMedia` point keyed by the parameter's own name. The refusal names the point and addresses the exact parameter through the JSON Pointer the contract fixes, so a resolver knows which value it is being asked for.

A supplied `emptyValueForm` outside the point's closed admissible set is an invalid caller choice, not an awaited one. Invocation therefore refuses plainly before dispatch; it is not context-required while that value stands.

A supplied empty string at a `query` parameter with `allowEmptyValue` absent refuses because the declaration does not admit an empty value at all. No configuration point and no credential repairs that, so §3.2's plain species applies and the refusal names nothing. This is the boundary the context-required species must not cross: the same empty value, one declaration apart, and only one of the two is awaiting anything.

Strict-JSON response parsing resolves duplicate object member names by taking the last member in document order — the last one the parse encounters, never an ordering of the names themselves — inside RFC 8259 Section 4's permitted receiver set. The 2.0-line twin of OAPI31-PS-118, asserted with a body whose duplicated names are in descending lexical order so that document order and lexical order cannot both be satisfied.
A leading byte-order mark on a JSON response body is ignored under RFC 8259 Section 8.1's parser latitude and is never part of the value. The 2.0-line twin of OAPI31-PS-121.

A lone-surrogate escape in a JSON response body yields no value and is a loud response-phase protocol error after a 2xx final status. The request direction is isolated by OAPI20-PS-180 through revision 4's lossless caller-input materialization.

Target construction performs one and only one seam repair: it removes the trailing base slash paired with the first leading Paths-key slash. An authored basePath of / and a Paths key beginning // therefore retain the key's intentional doubled slash.

Content-coding implementations are runtime capabilities, not binding configuration points. The actual Content-Encoding field fixes the coding stack even when the governing Response declares no Header Object for it. An absent declaration therefore imposes no content-coding constraint and does not declare identity; the runtime decoder removes the coding before the selected media lane.
OAS 2.0 does not forbid a path-template expression from occurring more than once. Its one effective path parameter supplies the same value at every occurrence.
An effective path parameter with no corresponding path-template expression is upstream-invalid and removes the selected target as invalid.

An API-key security alternative whose declared header destination is not an HTTP token is excluded before any credential value is inspected; the addressable target therefore refuses before dispatch rather than handing an invalid field name to an HTTP stack.
A 204 response cannot carry content. Even when the Response Object declares a schema, actual response bytes are a loud protocol error; the declaration never licenses decoding or an output value.
A non-token optional ordinary Header Parameter is excluded only at that projection; omitting it leaves the operation dispatchable.
The would-be caller key of an excluded optional non-token Header Parameter is unknown input and refuses before dispatch.
A non-token required ordinary Header Parameter excludes its addressable target, whose invocation refuses before dispatch.
An ordinary Header Parameter cannot give the caller control of Transfer-Encoding; the addressable target is excluded and refuses before dispatch.
A 101 response is an immediate loud response-phase protocol error because this unary binding has no upgraded-protocol continuation; the processor does not wait for another HTTP response.
A default-only Responses Object is valid, and its fallback Response Object governs an otherwise unmatched successful status.
A leading SP is field-line whitespace rather than part of an RFC 9110 field-value, so an ordinary Header Parameter cannot preserve it and refuses before dispatch.
A raw Cookie Header Parameter must serialize to a complete RFC 6265 cookie-string; a value without a cookie-pair refuses before dispatch.
A header apiKey credential ending in HTAB is not an RFC 9110 field-value and refuses before dispatch.
A complete configured HTTPS URL satisfies the server requirement created by a WebSocket-only declaration and dispatches the otherwise unchanged operation.
ASCII-case variants denote one response field: one received field discharges the group and the complete Content-Encoding value satisfies every binding-understood finite constraint.
A required parameter collision excludes only its credential alternative; a non-colliding OR alternative remains selectable and both its credential and the required caller field dispatch.
An omitted optional parameter creates no collision; the selected credential emits once and dispatches.
Ordinary and credential query contributions form one unordered multiset while preserving each contribution's encoded bytes.
A configured HTTP URL containing userinfo is nonconforming and refuses before dispatch rather than obscuring the actual authority.
A present empty artifact host cannot produce an HTTP target with a nonempty authority and refuses before dispatch.
A generated multipart name uses UTF-8, emits qdtext literally, and escapes only DQUOTE and backslash with one quoted-pair.
A followed cross-origin redirect strips binding-selected header credentials and does not append the original query credential to the Location target.
Supplying request Content-Encoding on an invocation that emits no request representation refuses before dispatch.
A valid RFC 6750 b64token is carried exactly as one OAuth2 Authorization field.
An empty OAuth2 access token cannot satisfy b64token and refuses before dispatch.
A space inside an OAuth2 access token is outside b64token and refuses before dispatch.
CR/LF in an OAuth2 access token is outside b64token and refuses before dispatch without emitting a field.
An explicitly non-Bearer OAuth2 runtime token has no carriage under this identifier and refuses before dispatch.

HEAD carries a syntactically valid, declaration-admitted Content-Encoding field but no content octets. The installed Brotli decoder fails if called, so successful empty completion proves the method-based no-content rule does not invoke it.

A 304 response carries a syntactically valid, declaration-admitted Content-Encoding field but no content octets. A failing Brotli sentinel is installed, but the no-content rule does not invoke it. Because 304 is not successful, completion remains the native unsuccessful response.

A non-UTF-8 character request lane requires its direction-specific encoder. With no such runtime capability, encoding refuses before dispatch rather than being reported as a response error or silently substituted.

On a successful HEAD response, a mixed enum contributes only its string-valued members to the exact raw-string domain. The wire value 7 is therefore outside the identity-only domain; ignoring the declaration or stringifying the numeric enum member would incorrectly complete.

A successful HEAD response still validates Content-Encoding field grammar before the no-content rule suppresses decoding; a non-token coding-list member fails loudly even though no decoder is invoked.
A successful HEAD response still applies its governing exact raw-string Content-Encoding domain; gzip is outside the declared br domain and fails loudly without invoking a content decoder.

Request and response character codecs are independent directional capabilities. The request encoder is installed and permits dispatch, while the response decoder is a failing sentinel and therefore produces a loud response-phase error.

A 204 response carries a syntactically valid, declaration-admitted Content-Encoding field but no content octets. The installed Brotli decoder fails if called, so successful empty completion proves the status-based no-content rule does not invoke it.

Case-equivalent response Header declarations govern conjunctively rather than by first-key selection. The first identity domain admits the actual field, but the second br domain rejects it, so the response fails loudly.

Case-equivalent response Header declarations govern conjunctively rather than by last-key selection. The first br domain rejects the actual field, although the second identity domain admits it, so the response fails loudly.

A caller-supplied JSON request value containing one unpaired surrogate code unit refuses before dispatch. The corpus materializes U+D800 after parsing its JSON-safe template so neither U+FFFD replacement nor an emitted lone-surrogate escape can masquerade as the supplied value.

An excluded optional non-token header projection sharing its declared name with a surviving query parameter is removed before caller-key uniqueness is computed; the surviving query parameter therefore uses its unqualified key and dispatches.
Because the removed header projection does not activate qualified mode, the would-be qualified query key is unknown input and refuses before dispatch.

Every admitted response media alternative is advertised once at equal preference in deterministic normalized order, while a case-insensitive q parameter is confined to its excluded alternative and cannot become an Accept weight.

An effective OAS 2.0 Header Parameter whose name differs from Accept only by ASCII case retains ordinary ownership and suppresses generated response-media advertisement even when omitted, so a q-bearing produces range remains admitted and governs response matching rather than being excluded for an Accept field the binding will not generate.
An out-of-enum authored scheme is confined to that invalid alternative, so a valid HTTPS sibling selects itself and dispatches.
When an out-of-enum authored scheme is the only alternative, a complete configured HTTPS URL recovers the represented target without repairing or selecting the invalid declaration.
A present caller-envelope value that is not a JSON object is outside the closed envelope grammar and refuses before dispatch; it is never treated as a body value or parameter map.
